raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Makes `examples/tpu/grpo` (scripts, README and image) work with `verl-hardware-plugin` `main`, and prepares it for the plugin loading its vLLM patches through an entry point. Only `examples/tpu/grpo/` changes.

1. **Drop `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS`** from both scripts and the README. verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#55 removed the plugin's `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` workaround and relies on Ray (>= 2.59) assigning `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` to each actor; with the variable set, Ray assigns none and the trainer fails in `init_process_group` with `RuntimeError: create_process_group(): PjRtClient is not initialized.`
2. **Install the plugin with pip instead of shipping its source in `py_modules`**: `"pip": {"packages": ["verl-hardware-plugin @ git+https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin@main"], "pip_install_options": ["--no-deps"]}`. An installed package registers entry points; a directory on `sys.path` does not. verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#58 moves the vLLM patches to a `vllm.general_plugins` entry point and fails fast when it is missing. `--no-deps` keeps the image's torch/verl. The README also shows how to install a local checkout as a wheel (`${RAY_RUNTIME_ENV_CREATE_WORKING_DIR}`).

3. **Build the image on Ray 2.59 with torchtitan 0.3.0** (`Dockerfile`): plugin `main` needs Ray >= 2.59 (above) and supports torchtitan 0.3.0, so the base moves from `rayproject/ray:2.56.0-py312` to `2.59.0-py312` and torchtitan is installed from PyPI (`0.3.0`) instead of the google-pytorch fork at `f880cc73` (drops `/torchtitan`, `PYTHONPATH` and the fork-only `typeguard`/`spmd_types` pins). The other pins (torch, torch-tpu, tpu-sync, jax, libtpu, vLLM, vllm-torchtpu, transformers, TransferQueue) are unchanged.
4. **Pass build credentials as BuildKit secrets**: the build pulls the private `vllm-project/vllm-torchtpu` repository and `torch-tpu` from an authenticated index, which the previous `docker buildx build -t <IMAGE> ...` command had no credentials for. The `Dockerfile` now reads `GIT_AUTH_TOKEN.github.com` and `tpu_index_token` secrets (not stored in the image) and the README documents the command.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+tpu , https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

2x TPU v6e-8 on GKE (`NNODES_TRAINER=2 NNODES_ROLLOUT=2`), Qwen3-0.6B 5-step smoke test. Rows 1-4 use an existing image with Ray 2.59, torchtitan 0.3.0, torch-tpu 0.1.2, vLLM 0.29 + vllm-torchtpu; the last row uses an image built from this PR's `Dockerfile`. verl `main` and verl-hardware-plugin `main`.

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| `main` as is (README `RUNTIME_ENV`, `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS=1`) | Fails in trainer init: `create_process_group(): PjRtClient is not initialized` |
| Only `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` removed (plugin still via `py_modules`) | 5/5 steps |
| This PR's README `RUNTIME_ENV` verbatim (plugin `main` pip-installed from git with `--no-deps`) | 5/5 steps |
| README's local-checkout variant with verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin#58 built as a wheel | 5/5 steps; vLLM EngineCore and workers on both rollout hosts patched through the entry point |
| **Image built from this PR's `Dockerfile`** with the README build command (Ray 2.59.0, torchtitan 0.3.0), then this PR's README `RUNTIME_ENV` verbatim | 5/5 steps |


AI assistance (Jetski) was used to debug the failures, write the changes, run the TPU tests, and draft this description. The submitter reviewed every changed line.

 ## 5. Run
 
-Ray ships `verl` and `verl-hardware-plugin` (from `../verl-hardware-plugin`) to the cluster with every job:
+Ray ships `verl` to the cluster with every job and installs `verl-hardware-plugin` into the job's environment on every node. The plugin must be installed (not just put on `sys.path`, e.g. with `py_modules`): vLLM's EngineCore and worker processes load its TPU patches through a `vllm.general_plugins` entry point, which only an installed package registers. `--no-deps` keeps pip from replacing the image's `torch`, `verl` and other pinned packages.
 
 ```bash
 export RAY_ADDRESS=http://localhost:23333
-RUNTIME_ENV='{"py_modules": ["../verl-hardware-plugin/verl_hardware_plugin"], "excludes": [".git", ".venv"],
+RUNTIME_ENV='{"pip": {"packages": ["verl-hardware-plugin @ git+https://github.com/verl-project/verl-hardware-plugin@main"],
+    "pip_install_options": ["--no-deps"]},
+  "excludes": [".git", ".venv"],
   "env_vars": {"PYTHONPATH": ".", "PYTHONUNBUFFERED": "1", "VERL_PLATFORM": "tpu",
-    "VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES": "verl_hardware_plugin", "RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS": "1",
-    "RAY_OVERRIDE_JOB_RUNTIME_ENV": "1"}}'
+    "VERL_USE_EXTERNAL_MODULES": "verl_hardware_plugin", "RAY_OVERRIDE_JOB_RUNTIME_ENV": "1"}}'
 
 ray job submit --working-dir . --runtime-env-json "$RUNTIME_ENV" -- bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_0_6b_torchtitan.sh
 ray job submit --working-dir . --runtime-env-json "$RUNTIME_ENV" -- bash examples/tpu/grpo/run_qwen3_4b_torchtitan.sh
 ```
 
+To run a local checkout of the plugin instead (e.g. to test changes), build it as a wheel inside the `verl` checkout, which Ray uploads with the job, and install that wheel:
+
+```bash
+pip wheel --no-deps -w plugin_whl ../verl-hardware-plugin
+RUNTIME_ENV=$(echo "$RUNTIME_ENV" | sed 's#"verl-hardware-plugin @ git+[^"]*"#"${RAY_RUNTIME_ENV_CREATE_WORKING_DIR}/plugin_whl/verl_hardware_plugin-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"#')
+```
+
+Do not set `RAY_EXPERIMENTAL_NOSET_TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS`: the plugin relies on Ray (2.59 or later) assigning `TPU_VISIBLE_CHIPS` to each actor.
